bands.name: The Throne and the Seraphim

evidence.note: Isaiah directly places seraphim above the throne; comparing their unceasing cry with Revelation is a textual parallel, not an identification.

bands.line: Isaiah sees the Lord on a throne, high and lifted up, with six-winged seraphim above him crying "Holy, holy, holy" — the same unceasing cry John hears from the four living creatures around the throne.

bands.name: The Cherubim

evidence.note: The cited passages directly name cherubim at Eden, above the mercy seat, and as the living creatures associated with the divine throne.

bands.line: Cherubim bear God's throne — Ezekiel names his four living creatures as cherubim, David says God "rode on a cherub, and flew" — and they guard Eden's way with a flaming sword and overshadow the mercy seat with their wings.

bands.name: The Archangel and the Chief Princes

evidence.note: Archangel and chief prince are direct scriptural terms; placing them together as one tier is an editorial connection rather than a hierarchy stated in one passage.

bands.line: Scripture calls only Michael "the archangel" — "one of the chief princes" and "the great prince who stands for the children of your people" — and the Lord will descend with the voice of the archangel.

bands.name: The Messengers and the Hosts

evidence.note: Every description is direct, but gathering serving spirits, mighty ones, and the heavenly army into one functional band is this room's synthesis.

bands.line: The angels are "serving spirits, sent out to do service for the sake of those who will inherit salvation" — mighty ones who fulfill his word, armies who do his pleasure, a multitude of the heavenly army, innumerable multitudes.

bands.name: The Earth Between

evidence.note: The individual scenes are explicit; presenting earth as a middle realm between holy and hostile unseen activity is a visual and editorial synthesis.

bands.line: The earth stands between the unseen armies: when the servant's eyes are opened the mountain is full of horses and chariots of fire, strangers may be angels unawares, and the adversary walks around like a roaring lion.

bands.name: Principalities and Powers

evidence.note: The titles and hostile contexts are direct; treating every principality or national prince as the same fixed class of fallen angel goes beyond what the passages settle.

bands.line: Our wrestling is not against flesh and blood but against principalities, powers, and the world's rulers of the darkness of this age — a "prince of the power of the air," a "god of this world" who blinds minds, and in Daniel a "prince of the kingdom of Persia" who withstands God's messenger twenty-one days.

bands.name: The Unclean Spirits

evidence.note: The Gospel passages directly call them unclean spirits, report their recognition of Jesus, and describe their obedience when he commands them out.

bands.line: The unclean spirits know who Jesus is and obey when he commands them out; a spirit gone out of a man passes through waterless places, and may return with seven others more evil than itself.

bands.name: The Abyss

evidence.note: Each cited prison image is explicit, while arranging the abyss, Tartarus, and bonds under darkness as one band compares passages that use distinct language.

bands.line: Demons beg Jesus not to send them into the abyss — a locked, smoking pit whose king angel is named Abaddon in Hebrew and Apollyon in Greek — and the angels who sinned were "cast down to Tartarus" (the WEB's rendering in 2 Peter), kept in everlasting bonds under darkness for the judgment of the great day.

bands.name: The End: the Lake of Fire

evidence.note: Jesus and Revelation directly connect the devil and his angels with final fire and state the deceiver's defeat; the passages remain apocalyptic judgment texts.

bands.line: The eternal fire was "prepared for the devil and his angels," and the devil who deceived the nations is thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, tormented day and night forever and ever.

named.name: Michael
named.line: The only angel scripture calls archangel: one of the chief princes who stands for God's people against the princes of the nations, disputes with the devil over the body of Moses, and leads the war against the dragon in heaven.
named.quote: But Michael, the archangel, when contending with the devil and arguing about the body of Moses, dared not bring against him an abusive condemnation, but said, “May the Lord rebuke you!”

named.name: Gabriel
named.line: Stands in the presence of God and carries his announcements: he explains Daniel's visions and announces the births of John the Baptist and of Jesus.
named.quote: The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God. I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

named.name: Raphael
named.line: Sent to heal Tobit's blindness and to free Sarah from the evil spirit Asmodaeus; he travels with Tobias unrecognized, then reveals himself as one of the seven who go in before the glory of the Holy One.
named.quote: I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels which present the prayers of the saints and go in before the glory of the Holy One.”
named.canonNote: Raphael appears only in Tobit — in the Catholic, Orthodox, Armenian, and Ethiopian canons on this site; not in the Hebrew Bible or the Protestant Old Testament.

named.name: Uriel
named.line: The angel sent to answer Ezra's questions about God's justice — and to humble him: he cannot comprehend even this world, let alone the way of the Most High.
named.quote: The angel who was sent to me, whose name was Uriel, gave me an answer,
named.canonNote: Uriel appears only in 2 Esdras, which sits outside most canons — printed as an appendix to the Latin Vulgate and read in the Slavonic and Ethiopian traditions; hosted here in the WEB apocrypha.

named.name: Raguel
named.meaning: Friend of God — the same name Exodus gives Moses' father-in-law, Reuel.
named.line: One of the seven holy angels who watch, set over the world of the luminaries — the lights of heaven. Two chapters later he is the angel at Enoch's side explaining the fire in the west.
named.quote: Then Raguel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered me
named.canonNote: Named only in 1 Enoch, canonical in the Ethiopian Orthodox church and outside every other canon; hosted here in R. H. Charles's 1917 translation.

named.name: Saraqâêl
named.meaning: The sense is uncertain; the name is also read as Sariel or Suriel. A Sariêl stands in the list of the Watchers' fallen leaders, and the text does not say whether the two are one.
named.line: One of the seven holy angels who watch, set over the spirits who sin in the spirit. This single verse is all the book says of him.
named.quote: Saraqâêl, one of the holy angels, who is set over the spirits, who sin in the spirit.
named.canonNote: Named only in 1 Enoch, canonical in the Ethiopian Orthodox church and outside every other canon; hosted here in R. H. Charles's 1917 translation.

named.name: Remiel
named.meaning: Read as mercy of God or thunder of God. A Râmîêl also stands among the fallen leaders in chapter 6; the book does not connect them.
named.line: The last of the seven holy angels who watch, set over those who rise — the resurrection.
named.quote: Remiel, one of the holy angels, whom God set over those who rise.
named.canonNote: Named only in 1 Enoch, canonical in the Ethiopian Orthodox church and outside every other canon; hosted here in R. H. Charles's 1917 translation.

named.name: Phanuel
named.meaning: Face of God — the Hebrew Peniel, the name Jacob gave the place where he wrestled.
named.line: The fourth of the four presences in the Parables of Enoch, set over the repentance of those who inherit eternal life. He stands with Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael to cast the fallen into the furnace, and goes in and out of the house of the Head of Days.
named.quote: and the fourth, who is set over the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel.
named.canonNote: Named only in 1 Enoch, canonical in the Ethiopian Orthodox church and outside every other canon; hosted here in R. H. Charles's 1917 translation.

named.name: The Angel of the LORD
named.meaning: Hebrew mal'akh YHWH — "messenger of Yahweh" (WEB: "Yahweh's angel")
named.line: Appears to Hagar, to Moses in the burning bush, to Gideon, and to Manoah — and the text sometimes speaks of him as God himself: Hagar "called the name of Yahweh who spoke to her," and Manoah says "we have seen God." Traditions read this differently — a manifestation of God, the pre-incarnate Christ, or a messenger speaking wholly in his sender's name.
named.quote: She called the name of Yahweh who spoke to her, “You are a God who sees,” for she said, “Have I even stayed alive after seeing him?”
named.canonNote: A special case, not a personal name: whether the Angel of the LORD is a created angel or God appearing is an interpretive question the text itself leaves open.

enemyNames.title: Satan — the adversary (Hebrew has the article, ha-satan: a title, "the accuser")
enemyNames.quote: Now on the day when God’s sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, Satan also came among them.

enemyNames.title: The devil
enemyNames.quote: Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.

enemyNames.title: Beelzebul
enemyNames.quote: “He has Beelzebul,” and, “By the prince of the demons he casts out the demons.”

enemyNames.title: The great dragon, the old serpent, the deceiver
enemyNames.quote: The great dragon was thrown down, the old serpent, he who is called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world.

enemyNames.title: The accuser
enemyNames.quote: the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, who accuses them before our God day and night.

enemyNames.title: The father of lies
enemyNames.quote: When he speaks a lie, he speaks on his own; for he is a liar, and the father of lies.

enemyNames.title: Murderer from the beginning
enemyNames.quote: He was a murderer from the beginning, and doesn’t stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him.

enemyNames.title: The prince of the power of the air
enemyNames.quote: according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit who now works in the children of disobedience.

enemyNames.title: The god of this world (WEB's phrase; often rendered "god of this age")
enemyNames.quote: in whom the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelieving

enemyNames.title: Abaddon / Apollyon — the angel of the abyss (the text names him king of the pit; it does not itself equate him with Satan)
enemyNames.quote: They have over them as king the angel of the abyss. His name in Hebrew is “Abaddon”, but in Greek, he has the name “Apollyon”.

enemyNames.title: The tempter
enemyNames.quote: The tempter came and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command that these stones become bread.”

enemyNames.title: A roaring lion
enemyNames.quote: Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.

enemyNames.title: An angel of light (a masquerade, not a nature)
enemyNames.quote: And no wonder, for even Satan masquerades as an angel of light.
